assumptions.condition: There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that \(c\le p'/p\le C\) \(\nu\)-almost everywhere for every \(P'\in\mathcal V_P\).

novel.justification: This nonstandard bounded likelihood-ratio chart is directly verifiable on two regimes: a positive finite-support simplex restricted away from its boundary, including the displayed \(36\)-cell chart, and a genuinely nonfinite bounded exponential-tilt family \(p_\eta/p=\exp\{\eta^\top g-\psi(\eta)\}\) with bounded measurable \(g\) and \(\eta\) in a sufficiently small compact neighborhood. It deliberately excludes generic dominated DQM paths with uncontrolled likelihood ratios.

assumptions.condition: \(\|\widetilde T_a(P')-\widetilde T_a(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to0\) as \(P'\to P\) in Hellinger distance for \(a=0,1\).

novel.justification: This fixed-coordinate continuity holds for positive finite-proxy charts and for conditional finite-matrix models with continuously varying cell laws; it permits moving marginal Hilbert spaces without selecting a bridge.

assumptions.condition: \(\dim\ker\widetilde T_a(P')=\dim\ker\widetilde T_a(P)\) for every \(P'\in\mathcal V_P\) and \(a=0,1\).

novel.justification: Fixed nullity describes the ordinary positive finite-proxy rank charts used in redundant-proxy applications while retaining nonzero null spaces.

assumptions.condition: \(\dim\ker\widetilde T_a(P')^*=\dim\ker\widetilde T_a(P)^*\) for every \(P'\in\mathcal V_P\) and \(a=0,1\).

novel.justification: Fixed cokernel dimension is satisfied away from singular-value crossings in finite categorical and fiberwise finite-proxy designs and allows treatment bridges to remain nonunique.

A uniform positive reduced minimum modulus is the spectral-gap property of positive finite rank charts and fiberwise matrix models; it guarantees closed range without imposing injectivity or surjectivity.

standard.name: Latent exchangeability with outcome negative-control exposure

assumptions.condition: Uniformly over folds, arms, and retained outcome-grid indices, \(\|\widehat h_{aj}^{(-k)}-h^0_{aj}\|_2=O_p(e_{h,2,n})\) and \(\|\widehat h_{aj}^{(-k)}-h^0_{aj}\|_4=O_p(e_{h,4,n})\).
Uniformly over folds, arms, and retained treatment-grid indices, \(\|\widehat q_{a\ell}^{(-k)}-q^0_{a\ell}\|_2=O_p(e_{q,2,n})\) and \(\|\widehat q_{a\ell}^{(-k)}-q^0_{a\ell}\|_4=O_p(e_{q,4,n})\).
Uniformly over folds, arms, and retained outcome-grid indices, \(\|T_a(\widehat h_{aj}^{(-k)}-h^0_{aj})\|_2=O_p(r_{h,n})\).
Uniformly over folds, arms, and retained treatment-grid indices, \(\|T_a^*(\widehat q_{a\ell}^{(-k)}-q^0_{a\ell})\|_2=O_p(r_{q,n})\).

Foldwise, \(\|\widehat E_{-k}[\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k)}\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k)\top}]-E[D^0_{J_n}D_{J_n}^{0\top}]\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_p(\eta_{G,n})\) and \(\|\widehat E_{-k}[\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k)}\sum_{a=0}^1t_aS_a(\widehat h_{a0}^{(-k)},\widehat q_{a0}^{(-k)})]-E[D^0_{J_n}\sum_{a=0}^1t_aS_a(h^0_{a0},q^0_{a0})]\|_2=O_p(\eta_{c,n})\), where \((\eta_{G,n}+\eta_{c,n})/\kappa_{J_n}=o(1)\).

Foldwise, \(\sum_{j=0}^{J_n^h}\sum_{\ell=0}^{J_n^q}\widehat\lambda_{a,j\ell}^{(-k)}=\sum_{j=0}^{J_n^h}\sum_{\ell=0}^{J_n^q}\lambda^0_{a,j\ell}=1\) for each arm, and \(\sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{j=0}^{J_n^h}\sum_{\ell=0}^{J_n^q}(|\widehat\lambda_{a,j\ell}^{(-k)}|+|\lambda^0_{a,j\ell}|)\le L_n\).

novel.justification: Exact affine centering and a controlled coefficient envelope are directly enforceable linear constraints in the finite convex projection program and do not select a preferred bridge.

This balance permits growing affine dictionaries while exposing approximation, learned-dictionary, empirical inversion, and ridge errors separately; smooth conditional finite-matrix models with dimension fixed or slowly growing satisfy it.

assumptions.condition: For every fold \(k\), each fitted bridge \(\widehat h_{aj}^{(-k)}\), \(\widehat q_{a\ell}^{(-k)}\), each evaluated bridge-dictionary coordinate, and each resulting scalar weight are measurable with respect to \(\mathcal D_{-k}\).

Uniformly over folds and retained bridge cells, the held-out cell signals and adjusted signal defined in \(\mathrm{def:affine-ensemble-estimator}\) are square-integrable conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{-k}\) with probability tending to one.

definitions.name: transported bounded-ratio fixed-rank closed-range chart
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal U_P=\{P'\in\mathcal V_P:c\le p'/p\le C,\ \widetilde T_a(P')=J_{G,a}(P')T_a(P')J_W(P')^{-1}\text{ varies continuously in operator norm},\ \dim\ker\widetilde T_a(P')\text{ and }\dim\ker\widetilde T_a(P')^*\text{ equal their base-law values},\ \mu_a(P')\ge\underline\mu_a,\ a=0,1\}\). The chart domain \(\mathcal V_P\) is not asserted to be Hellinger-open.

definitions.name: local joint nonunique proximal bridge chart
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{joint}}(P)=\mathcal L_{\mathrm{out}}(P)\cap\mathcal L_{\mathrm{trt}}(P)\) inside the deliberately restricted bounded likelihood-ratio domain \(\mathcal V_P\). Its admissible paths are every DQM/Hellinger differentiable \(t\mapsto P_t\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{joint}}(P)\) with \(P_0=P\), \(c\le p_t/p\le C\) for sufficiently small \(t\), and \(\sqrt{p_t}=\sqrt p(1+ts/2)+o(t)\) in \(L^2(\nu)\) for some \(s\in L_0^2(P)\). No differentiable bridge representative is included in the definition of a path.

definitions.name: valid bridge doubly robust score family
three-class observable normal space
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_P=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{F_a(h,m),G_a(q,u),R_a(m,u):a\in\{0,1\},\ h\in\mathcal H_a(P),\ q\in\mathcal Q_a(P),\ m\in\mathcal K_a(P),\ u\in\mathcal N_a(P),\ F_a,G_a,R_a\in L_0^2(P)\}\).

definitions.name: coupled score-lifting handle
definitions.construction: Linearize the joint outcome-solvability, treatment-solvability, and moving-rank maps; quotient their derivative by \(\mathcal N_a(P)\) and \(\mathcal K_a(P)\); orthogonalize the two arms' derivative equations against the shared \((W,X)\) marginal; and use closed-range right inverses plus finite-support chart localization to synthesize path-score approximants for a target element of \(\mathcal C_P^\perp\).

definitions.name: strictly positive nonattainment witness
definitions.construction: Let \(X\) be absent, \(U^\star\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), \(P^\star(A=1\mid U^\star=u)=(1+2u)/4\), and let \(Z,W\in\{0,1,2\}\) be conditionally independent given \(U^\star\), each with probability vector \((3/5,3/10,1/10)\) at \(U^\star=0\) and \((1/10,3/10,3/5)\) at \(U^\star=1\). Given \((A,U^\star)\), let \(Y\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/5+A/5+2U^\star/5)\), conditionally independent of \((Z,W)\). The observed marginal law is \(P^\star\).

definitions.name: finite positive rank-two joint constraint map
definitions.construction: For \(Z,W\in\{0,1,2\}\), choose a nonsingular rank-two minor \(C_a\) and partition \(B_a=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}C_a&D_a\\E_a&F_a^{B}\end{smallmatrix}\right]\), \(b_a=(b_{a,\mathrm{top}},b_{a,\mathrm{bot}})\), and \(d=(d_{\mathrm{top}},d_{\mathrm{bot}})\). Define \(\Xi(P)=\{F_a^{B}-E_aC_a^{-1}D_a,\ b_{a,\mathrm{bot}}-E_aC_a^{-1}b_{a,\mathrm{top}},\ d_{\mathrm{bot}}-D_a^\top C_a^{-\top}d_{\mathrm{top}}:a=0,1\}\), with the same marginal vector \(d\) in both arms.

definitions.name: transported Chen--Xie outcome-only comparator model
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CX}}(P)=\mathcal U_P\cap\mathcal L_{\mathrm{out}}(P)\), with every DQM path in this intersection admissible and with target \(\theta(P)=E[h_1(W,X)-h_0(W,X)]\). The treatment-solvability locus is not imposed.

definitions.name: population bridge and normal dictionaries
definitions.construction: Choose \(h^0_{aj}\in\mathcal H_a(P)\), \(j=0,\ldots,J_n^h\), and \(q^0_{a\ell}\in\mathcal Q_a(P)\), \(\ell=0,\ldots,J_n^q\), taking the base cell so that \(\phi_0=\sum_{a=0}^1t_aS_a(h^0_{a0},q^0_{a0})-\theta(P)\). Put \(S^0_{a,j\ell}=S_a(h^0_{aj},q^0_{a\ell})\) and concatenate \(D^{h,0}_{a,j}=t_a(S^0_{a,j0}-S^0_{a,00})\), \(D^{q,0}_{a,\ell}=t_a(S^0_{a,0\ell}-S^0_{a,00})\), and \(D^{hq,0}_{a,j\ell}=t_a(S^0_{a,j\ell}-S^0_{a,j0}-S^0_{a,0\ell}+S^0_{a,00})\) into \(D^0_{J_n}\). Define \(b_{J_n}=\arg\min_bE[(\phi_0-b^\top D^0_{J_n})^2]\) on the nonzero Gram eigenspace, \(\kappa_{J_n}=\lambda_{\min}^{+}E[D^0_{J_n}D_{J_n}^{0\top}]\), and \(\alpha_{J_n}=\inf_b\|\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0-b^\top D^0_{J_n}\|_2\).

definitions.name: cross-fitted penalized-minimax Galerkin affine ensemble
definitions.construction: For each fold \(k\), use only \(\mathcal D_{-k}\) to fit \(\widehat h_{aj}^{(-k)}\), \(j=0,\ldots,J_n^h\), and \(\widehat q_{a\ell}^{(-k)}\), \(\ell=0,\ldots,J_n^q\), and put \(\widehat S_{a,j\ell}^{(-k)}=S_a(\widehat h_{aj}^{(-k)},\widehat q_{a\ell}^{(-k)})\) and \(\widehat B^{(-k)}=\sum_{a=0}^1t_a\widehat S_{a,00}^{(-k)}\). For each arm form \(\widehat D^h_{a,j}=t_a(\widehat S_{a,j0}^{(-k)}-\widehat S_{a,00}^{(-k)})\), \(\widehat D^q_{a,\ell}=t_a(\widehat S_{a,0\ell}^{(-k)}-\widehat S_{a,00}^{(-k)})\), and \(\widehat D^{hq}_{a,j\ell}=t_a(\widehat S_{a,j\ell}^{(-k)}-\widehat S_{a,j0}^{(-k)}-\widehat S_{a,0\ell}^{(-k)}+\widehat S_{a,00}^{(-k)})\), and concatenate them as \(\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k)}\). The training Gram and cross-moment are \(\widehat G^{(-k)}=\widehat E_{-k}[\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k)}\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k)\top}]\) and \(\widehat c^{(-k)}=\widehat E_{-k}[\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k)}\widehat B^{(-k)}]\), and \(\widehat b^{(-k)}=(\widehat G^{(-k)}+\rho_nI)^{-1}\widehat c^{(-k)}\) is unique because \(\rho_n>0\). Partition \(\widehat b^{(-k)}=(\widehat b^h,\widehat b^q,\widehat b^{hq})\) and define scalar weights by \(\widehat\lambda_{a,j\ell}=-\widehat b^{hq}_{a,j\ell}\), \(\widehat\lambda_{a,j0}=-\widehat b^h_{a,j}+\sum_{\ell=1}^{J_n^q}\widehat b^{hq}_{a,j\ell}\), \(\widehat\lambda_{a,0\ell}=-\widehat b^q_{a,\ell}+\sum_{j=1}^{J_n^h}\widehat b^{hq}_{a,j\ell}\), and \(\widehat\lambda_{a,00}=1+\sum_{j=1}^{J_n^h}\widehat b^h_{a,j}+\sum_{\ell=1}^{J_n^q}\widehat b^q_{a,\ell}-\sum_{j=1}^{J_n^h}\sum_{\ell=1}^{J_n^q}\widehat b^{hq}_{a,j\ell}\). Direct collection of coefficients gives \(\sum_{j=0}^{J_n^h}\sum_{\ell=0}^{J_n^q}\widehat\lambda_{a,j\ell}=1\) and \(\sum_a t_a\sum_{j,\ell}\widehat\lambda_{a,j\ell}\widehat S_{a,j\ell}^{(-k)}=\widehat B^{(-k)}-\widehat b^{(-k)\top}\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k)}\). The map from \(\widehat b^{(-k)}\) to the weights is deterministic and Borel. For \(i\in\mathcal I_k\), set \(\widehat\psi_i=\sum_a t_a\sum_{j,\ell}\widehat\lambda_{a,j\ell}^{(-k)}\widehat S_{a,j\ell}^{(-k)}(O_i)\), \(\widehat\theta_n=n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\psi_i\), and \(\widehat V_n=n^{-1}\sum_i(\widehat\psi_i-\widehat\theta_n)^2\). Conditional on \(\mathcal D_{-k}\), all fitted objects use training data only and are independent of the i.i.d. held-out observations; the retained held-out signals are square-integrable under \(\mathrm{ass:heldout-signal-integrability}\).

definitions.name: learned-projection and mixed-bias gauges
definitions.construction: Let \(\delta_{D,n}=O_p\{B_{J_n}(e_{h,4,n}+e_{q,4,n})+e_{h,4,n}e_{q,4,n}\}\), \(b_{\rho,n}=\rho_n\|b_{J_n}\|_2/\kappa_{J_n}\), and let \(\eta_{G,n}\) and \(\eta_{c,n}\) bound the foldwise empirical Gram and score--dictionary cross-moment perturbations. The primitive mixed-bias gauge is \(L_n\min\{r_{h,n}e_{q,2,n},r_{q,n}e_{h,2,n}\}\).

statements.statement: For every \(a\), \(h\in\mathcal H_a(P)\), \(q\in\mathcal Q_a(P)\), \(u\in\mathcal N_a(P)\), and \(m\in\mathcal K_a(P)\) on the square-integrable product domain, \[S_a(h+u,q+m)-S_a(h,q)=F_a(h,m)-G_a(q,u)-R_a(m,u).\] Pure shifts and the four-corner contrast recover the three terms separately, so \[\mathcal C_P=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{\phi-\phi':\phi,\phi'\in\Phi_P\}\quad\text{and}\quad\mathcal A_P=\phi_0+\mathcal C_P\] for every \(\phi_0\in\Phi_P\).
statements.justification: The identity isolates the interaction normal missed by optimizing over one bridge coordinate at a time.
statements.gap: BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified proves the mixed-bias identity for a fixed primal-dual pair; it does not identify the closed affine geometry generated by all nonunique proximal pairs.
statements.consumer: The identity converts a normal-equation projection into an implementable affine ensemble of ordinary proximal doubly robust signals.

statements.statement: Let \(A,A':\mathcal H\to\mathcal G_a\) have closed range, reduced minimum moduli at least \(\mu>0\), and \(\varepsilon=\|A'-A\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\mu\). Then \[\operatorname{gap}(\ker A',\ker A)\le\varepsilon/\mu,\qquad \operatorname{gap}(\ker A'^*,\ker A^*)\le\varepsilon/\mu.\] With the symmetric gap convention for closed subspaces, the same bounds control the norms of the associated orthogonal-projection differences. Applied to \(A=\widetilde T_a(P)\) and \(A'=\widetilde T_a(P')\), operator-norm continuity and the uniform reduced-modulus bound therefore imply \(\|\widetilde\Pi_{N,a}(P')-\widetilde\Pi_{N,a}(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to0\) and \(\|\widetilde\Pi_{K,a}(P')-\widetilde\Pi_{K,a}(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to0\). When these projections have finite rank, a bound below one also forces equality of their ranks, so fixed nullity and cokernel are locally redundant labels on such a component. No differentiability of projections or bridge selections, solvability-submanifold claim, or path-score realization follows from these bounds.
statements.justification: The perturbation bound derives moving kernel and cokernel continuity from the spectral gap instead of maintaining those conclusions as assumptions.
statements.gap: Standard closed-range perturbation arguments control subspace gaps, but they do not solve the proposal's reverse path-score lifting problem.
statements.consumer: The lemma supplies stable transported null-space coordinates for the score-lifting construction and the finite-chart continuity arguments.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathrm{def:score-lifting-handle}\), can one prove for every base law \(P\) in the transported bounded likelihood-ratio joint chart that each \(s\in\mathcal C_P^\perp\) is an \(L^2(P)\) limit of finite linear combinations of scores of actual DQM paths \(t\mapsto P_t\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{joint}}(P)\) that remain in the bounded-ratio domain, with \(\sqrt{p_t}=\sqrt p(1+ts/2)+o(t)\), including moving kernels, genuine treatment-solvability, and the shared \((W,X)\) marginal, and hence that \(\mathcal T_P=\mathcal C_P^\perp\) for this actual restricted path class?
statements.justification: This reverse inclusion remains the load-bearing open obligation for the actual bounded likelihood-ratio path class; neither operator perturbation nor differentiated solvability equations constructs the required paths.
statements.gap: ChenSantos2018Overidentification and ChenXie2026LocalOveridentification give range-versus-annihilator arguments for outcome conditional moments, but not score lifting for the intersection of outcome and adjoint solvability loci with moving kernels and a shared marginal.
statements.consumer: A positive answer determines the legitimate information bound for every regular estimator in the joint nonunique-bridge model.

statements.statement: Under the latent-extension assumptions, \(h_a^\dagger\) satisfies \(E[Y\mid A=a,Z,X]=E[h_a^\dagger(W,X)\mid A=a,Z,X]\). Hence \(h_a^\dagger\in\mathcal H_a(P)\). If treatment bridges exist, then every \(h_a\in\mathcal H_a(P)\) has \(E[h_a(W,X)]=E[h_a^\dagger(W,X)]=E[Y(a)]\), and therefore the observed joint-bridge functional obeys \(\theta(P)=E[Y(1)-Y(0)]\).
statements.justification: This proposition separates an observed-law efficiency problem from the assumptions needed to interpret its target as an ATE.
statements.gap: MiaoGengTchetgen2018Proxy gives proximal causal identification; the proposition records exactly which latent extension makes the observed joint-bridge functional causal without adding bridge uniqueness or completeness.
statements.consumer: The SUPPORT analysis may invoke the quotient efficiency results for an ATE only after checking this proximal causal interpretation.

statements.statement: For \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{joint}}(P)\), conditional on proving \(\mathrm{oeq:score-lifting-completeness}\), the observed joint-bridge functional \(\theta\) is pathwise differentiable if and only if \(\Phi_P\neq\varnothing\). Whenever this holds, every gradient lies in \(\mathcal A_P\) and \[\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}=\phi_0-\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\varphi\in\mathcal A_P}E[\varphi^2],\qquad V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=\inf_{\varphi\in\mathcal A_P}E[\varphi^2].\] The claim is not unconditional: the projection becomes the canonical gradient only after the reverse score-lifting inclusion is established.
statements.justification: Conditional on the explicit reverse-inclusion obligation, this identifies the regularity frontier and global canonical gradient across all bridge pairs in the simultaneous-existence observed-law model.
statements.gap: ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness already supplies root-\(n\), regular, asymptotically linear nonunique-bridge estimation and local semiparametric efficiency under additional regularity; BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified supplies regular selected-pair inference. Neither result proves the complete tangent and normal geometry or the global affine-hull bound when both bridge-existence restrictions define the observed model.
statements.consumer: Analysts with redundant proxies can distinguish a valid selected-pair standard error from the global joint-model information bound.

statements.statement: Conditional on \(\mathrm{oeq:score-lifting-completeness}\), fix \(\phi_0=\phi_{h,q}\in\Phi_P\). A shifted pair \((h_a+u_a,q_a+m_a)_{a=0}^1\) attains \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\) if and only if there are \(u_a\in\mathcal N_a(P)\) and \(m_a\in\mathcal K_a(P)\) such that \[\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0=\sum_{a=0}^1t_a\{-F_a(h_a,m_a)+G_a(q_a,u_a)+R_a(m_a,u_a)\}.\] Otherwise every single-pair score has variance strictly above the affine-hull bound, while four-corner affine ensembles can approximate it.
statements.justification: The factorization equation determines when choosing one representative can equal global across-pair efficiency.
statements.gap: ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness establishes locally efficient regular inference under its additional regularity, while CuiEtAl2024SemiparametricProximal obtains single-pair efficiency under uniqueness and surjectivity; neither gives this two-fiber attainment criterion.
statements.consumer: The SUPPORT workflow can test whether fitted bridge scores leave variance-reducing affine directions.

statements.statement: The law \(P^\star\) lies in the joint chart, has positive mass on all \(36\) observed cells, and has rank-two arm operators with \(\mathcal N_a(P^\star)=\mathcal K_a(P^\star)=\operatorname{span}\{(3,-7,3)^\top\}\). For the displayed constraint map \(\Xi\), the Jacobian has constant full row rank on a relatively open positive neighborhood of \(P^\star\); only on this finite chart the joint solvability locus is thereby proved to be a submanifold, with \(\mathcal T_P=\mathcal C_P^\perp\). At \(P^\star\), \(\theta(P^\star)=1/5\), \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^\star)=773723312/334026875\), and the exact coefficient obstruction \(410302072/87437547015>0\) in each arm implies that no single bridge pair attains the bound. The strict nonattainment persists on a smaller relatively open chart.
statements.justification: The exact chart supplies a fully path-based local witness that affine enlargement is substantive rather than a formal projection choice.
statements.gap: BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified allows pair-dependent scores but gives no positive regular chart on which every individual pair is inefficient relative to the actual canonical gradient.
statements.consumer: The witness is a reproducible early-kill test for tangent formulas and affine-ensemble implementations.

statements.statement: At \(P^\star\), the displayed selected functions solve \(T_ah_a^{\mathrm{sel}}=g_a\) and \(T_a^*q_a^{\mathrm{sel}}=1\), and the positive finite law satisfies the bounded-moment, adjoint-range, stable-selection, and product-rate hypotheses used by ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness Theorem \(3.4\) and Corollary \(B.1\), as well as the selected-limit conditions of BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified Theorems \(3\), \(6\), and \(7\). Thus the Zhang estimator is root-\(n\), regular, asymptotically linear, and locally semiparametrically efficient on its additional-regularity model, and the Bennett construction is regular and asymptotically linear for the selected pair. On the joint positive rank-two chart, however, their selected-pair score obeys \[V_{\mathrm{sel}}=4432/1875=V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^\star)+9496288/200416125>V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^\star).\] Smooth bridge continuation and continuity of the normal Gram matrix preserve this strict gap on a relatively open neighborhood.
statements.justification: The exact inequality respects Zhang et al.'s existing local efficiency result while isolating the new comparison: global efficiency across bridge pairs in the smaller simultaneous-existence observed-law model.
statements.gap: ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness already proves root-\(n\), regular, asymptotically linear estimation and local semiparametric efficiency under additional regularity, and BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified proves regular selected-pair inference; neither computes the strictly smaller joint-model affine quotient variance on this assumption-matched positive chart.
statements.consumer: The SUPPORT workflow gains a certificate for when a valid locally efficient selected-bridge standard error is not variance-minimizing in the joint observed-law experiment.

statements.statement: In the transported coordinates, \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{joint}}(P)\subset\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CX}}(P)\), so \(\mathcal T_P\subseteq\mathcal T_{\mathrm{CX},P}\). Extend \(P^\star\) by taking \(Y(a,z)=Y(a)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/5+a/5+2U^\star/5)\) and \(W(a,z)=W\) for every \(a,z\), with \((Y(a),W)\perp(A,Z)\mid U^\star\). Together with bounded finite support, strict cell positivity, treatment probabilities \(1/4\) and \(3/4\), positive Bernoulli residual variances, the displayed outcome bridge, and full column rank of the binary-latent-to-three-level \(Z\) probability matrix, this verifies the negative-control exposure, negative-control outcome, latent ignorability, overlap, bridge, variance, and completeness hypotheses used for ChenXie2026LocalOveridentification Theorem \(3\). The target derivatives agree on the intersection because both targets equal \(E[h_1-h_0]\). Consequently \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P}\phi_{\mathrm{CX}}\) and \[V_{\mathrm{CX}}(P)-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=\|\Pi_{\mathcal T_{\mathrm{CX},P}\cap\mathcal T_P^\perp}\phi_{\mathrm{CX}}\|_2^2.\] The additional normal directions are the nonredundant components of \(\overline{\operatorname{span}}(G,R)\) modulo \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{out},P}\). Exact projection at \(P^\star\) gives \(V_{\mathrm{CX}}(P^\star)=71536/30625\) and \(V_{\mathrm{CX}}(P^\star)-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^\star)=1303968/66805375>0\).
statements.justification: This assumption-matched projection identity isolates the efficiency gain from genuine treatment-bridge solvability rather than comparing formulas across nonnested models.
statements.gap: ChenXie2026LocalOveridentification Theorem \(3\) computes the canonical gradient for the outcome-bridge-only negative-control model; it does not impose or exploit simultaneous adjoint bridge solvability, whose nonredundant normals yield the exact positive gap above.
statements.consumer: The comparison tells negative-control analysts when imposing an empirically credible treatment-bridge existence restriction changes the attainable variance.

statements.statement: Under the population dictionary, training measurability, conditional square-integrability, and bridge-rate conditions, the explicitly constructed fold dictionaries satisfy \[\max_k\|\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k)}-D^0_{J_n}\|_{L^2(P)}=O_p(\delta_{D,n}),\qquad \delta_{D,n}=O_p\{B_{J_n}(e_{h,4,n}+e_{q,4,n})+e_{h,4,n}e_{q,4,n}\}.\] Conditional on \(\mathcal D_{-k}\), training/holdout independence and the fourth-moment growth condition give \(\eta_{G,n}=O_p\{J_nB_{J_n}^2\sqrt{\log(1+J_n)/n}+\sqrt{J_n}B_{J_n}\delta_{D,n}+J_n\delta_{D,n}^2\}\) and \(\eta_{c,n}=O_p\{\sqrt{J_n}B_{J_n}^2\sqrt{\log(1+J_n)/n}+\sqrt{J_n}B_{J_n}\delta_{D,n}\}\). The positive ridge makes every fold coefficient unique, and resolvent perturbation gives \[\max_k\|\widehat b^{(-k)\top}\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k)}-\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0\|_2=O_p\!\left(\alpha_{J_n}+L_n\delta_{D,n}+\frac{\eta_{G,n}+\eta_{c,n}}{\kappa_{J_n}}+b_{\rho,n}\right)=o_p(1).\] The explicit deterministic coefficient-to-weight identity then yields \(\|\widehat\psi-\theta(P)-\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\|_2=o_p(1)\); this convergence is derived rather than assumed.
statements.justification: The lemma closes the feasible-projection step from primitive bridge, sieve, and empirical-moment rates rather than assuming the desired efficient signal.
statements.gap: AiChen2012SequentialMoments controls optimally weighted sieve moments and BennettEtAl2023SourceConditionDR controls one primal-dual score; neither derives an affine four-corner dictionary projection with learned nonunique bridge representatives.
statements.consumer: The lemma supplies checkable tuning and rate diagnostics for the SUPPORT affine-ensemble implementation.

statements.statement: Conditional on \(\mathrm{oeq:score-lifting-completeness}\), suppose \(0<V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)<\infty\), \(K_{\mathrm{fold}}\) is fixed, the primitive conditions of \(\mathrm{lem:learned-projection-convergence}\) hold along the base law and contiguous joint-chart paths, and \(\sqrt nL_n\min\{r_{h,n}e_{q,2,n},r_{q,n}e_{h,2,n}\}=o(1)\). Then \[\sqrt n\{\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P)\}=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_p(1)\Rightarrow N\{0,V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\},\] \(\widehat V_n/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\to_p1\), and \(P\{\theta(P)\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha\). The contiguous-path expansion makes the estimator regular and efficient for the observed joint-bridge functional.
statements.justification: The theorem converts the conditional quotient gradient into regular pointwise inference under explicit approximation, estimation, conditioning, envelope, ridge, and mixed-bias rates.
statements.gap: ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness already gives root-\(n\), regular, asymptotically linear and locally efficient selected-representative inference under additional regularity; BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified gives selected-limit inference, and AiShan2025EfficientProximalATE gives uniquely indexed GMM. None learns the global affine score projection across two nonunique bridge fibers.
statements.consumer: A SUPPORT reanalysis can report a variance-minimizing affine-ensemble standard error together with the selected-pair benchmark.

statements.statement: Conditional on \(\mathrm{oeq:score-lifting-completeness}\), if \(T_a\) and \(T_a^*\) are bijective for \(a=0,1\), then \(\mathcal N_a(P)=\mathcal K_a(P)=\{0\}\), \(\mathcal C_P=\{0\}\), \(\Phi_P=\{\phi_{h,q}\}\), and \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}=\phi_{h,q}\). Thus the quotient bound reduces to CuiEtAl2024SemiparametricProximal Theorem \(3.1\).
statements.justification: The reduction is the standard-case sanity check once the general score-lifting obligation is discharged.
statements.gap: CuiEtAl2024SemiparametricProximal establishes the unique-and-surjective endpoint; this theorem verifies exact nesting without imposing those restrictions on the main model.
statements.consumer: Existing proximal software remains efficiency-valid when diagnostics support unique bijective bridge operators.

sampling_model.design: Dominated i.i.d. observed-data experiment on a deliberately restricted bounded likelihood-ratio chart, with square-root-density transports to fixed Hilbert spaces, norm-continuous operators, fixed rank labels, and a uniform positive reduced minimum modulus. The chart is not claimed to be Hellinger-open or to preserve the unrestricted dominated tangent set.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment \(A_i\in\{0,1\}\). The main target is an observed joint-bridge functional; its ATE interpretation requires the separate latent-extension proposition.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment-bridge existence is a genuine observed solvability restriction. No injectivity, surjectivity, bridge uniqueness, completeness of an observed operator, or minimum-norm representative is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cross-fitted penalized-minimax or Galerkin learning of rectangular outcome--treatment bridge grids; fold-specific pure and four-corner contrasts; an explicit positive-ridge training Gram/cross-moment solution; and a deterministic scalar affine-weight map under approximation, fourth-moment, Gram, ridge, coefficient-envelope, and mixed-bias rates.

tldr: ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness already gives root-\(n\), regular, asymptotically linear nonunique-bridge estimation and local semiparametric efficiency under additional regularity, and BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified gives regular selected-pair inference. The new kernel concerns the local observed-law intersection in which outcome and treatment bridges must remain simultaneously solvable while both fibers may be non-singleton. On an explicit transported bounded likelihood-ratio fixed-rank closed-range chart, operator perturbation derives kernel and cokernel projection continuity, but score-lifting completeness for the actual restricted path class remains the load-bearing open obligation; only conditional on that result does the affine-hull projection become the canonical gradient and global bound across bridge pairs. A positive \(36\)-cell chart proves tangent equality locally, yields an exact strict Zhang--Bennett selected-pair gap, and gives an assumption-matched strict projection gap from ChenXie2026LocalOveridentification's outcome-only model. An explicitly fold-indexed ridge/Galerkin construction and primitive sieve, bridge-rate, Gram, envelope, and mixed-bias conditions imply learned efficient-signal convergence and feasible Wald inference. The main target is an observed joint-bridge functional; a separate latent-extension proposition identifies it with the ATE.

project_justification.gap: ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness already establishes root-\(n\), regular, asymptotically linear nonunique-bridge estimation and local semiparametric efficiency under additional regularity, BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified establishes regular selected-pair inference, and ChenXie2026LocalOveridentification computes efficiency in the outcome-bridge-only observed model. None characterizes the complete tangent closure of the joint observed-law intersection where outcome and treatment bridges remain simultaneously solvable, or its global canonical gradient across both nonunique fibers.
project_justification.niche: Treatment-bridge solvability can shrink the observed tangent space beyond the outcome-only model. Its nonredundant adjoint-solvability and null-interaction normals create an exact efficiency gain while preserving bridge nonuniqueness and avoiding a preferred representative.
project_justification.fill: The project defines an explicit transported bounded likelihood-ratio rank chart, derives projection continuity from operator perturbation, and keeps reverse score lifting for the actual restricted path class open rather than assuming it. Conditional on that obligation it derives the joint quotient gradient and attainment criterion; finite positive charts prove local submanifold status and exact Zhang--Bennett and Chen--Xie variance gaps, and a fully fold-indexed ridge construction with primitive learning conditions yields the affine-ensemble limit law.

related_work: MiaoGengTchetgen2018Proxy supplies the latent proximal conditions used only for the separate causal-identification proposition. ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness Theorem \(3.4\) already constructs a root-\(n\), regular, asymptotically linear estimator with nonunique bridges, and Corollary \(B.1\) establishes local semiparametric efficiency under additional regularity; the new claim is confined to complete tangent and normal geometry and global across-pair efficiency for the simultaneous-existence observed-law model. BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified Theorem \(3\) gives the all-pair mixed-bias identity and Theorems \(6\)--\(7\) give the penalized-minimax selected-limit inference architecture; the exact finite chart shows that a Zhang--Bennett selected-pair variance can strictly exceed the joint affine quotient bound without questioning validity or local efficiency in their maintained model. ChenXie2026LocalOveridentification Theorem \(3\) gives the generalized-inverse canonical gradient for the outcome-bridge-only negative-control model. The assumption-matched comparison nests the joint model inside that transported outcome-only model and identifies the added adjoint-solvability normals, with exact variance gap \(1303968/66805375\) at the positive witness. CuiEtAl2024SemiparametricProximal Theorem \(3.1\) is the unique-and-surjective endpoint. SeveriniTripathi2012EfficiencyBounds supplies the quotient-functional precedent, and ChenSantos2018Overidentification supplies the range-versus-annihilator framework. AiChen2012SequentialMoments informs Gram stabilization and sieve weighting. AiShan2025EfficientProximalATE informs increasing-moment implementation but maintains a uniquely indexed bridge. ImbensEtAl2025LongTerm concerns a distinct unique-bridge data-combination model. BennettEtAl2023SourceConditionDR supplies primitive inverse-problem residual and product-rate tools.
technical_internal_limitation: The reverse inclusion \(\mathcal T_P\supseteq\mathcal C_P^\perp\) is not an assumption and is not implied by differentiating either bridge equation or by the operator-perturbation lemma. It requires scores of actual DQM paths in the intersection of the two solvability loci, with transported moving kernels, a shared \((W,X)\) marginal, and the bounded likelihood-ratio restriction maintained along each path. The deliberately restricted chart is not Hellinger-open and does not preserve the unrestricted dominated tangent set; generic dominated DQM paths with uncontrolled likelihood ratios are outside this version. Verifiable chart regimes include a positive finite-support simplex away from its boundary, including the \(36\)-cell witness, and a nonfinite bounded exponential-tilt family with bounded statistics on a small compact parameter set. The general treatment-solvability locus is not called a submanifold; submanifold status is proved only on the finite positive chart through the displayed Schur-complement constraint map and its full-row-rank Jacobian. Separate square integrability of \(Y\), \(h\), and \(q\) does not ensure square integrability of their score product. Closed range excludes generic compact infinite-rank problems. The exact finite witness verifies the Chen--Xie hypotheses and strict gap, but general strictness requires nonzero additional normal projection. The final Bennett publisher text remained inaccessible with an HTTP \(403\) response on 2026-09-13, so that comparison uses the public manuscript plus publisher metadata.
honest_scope: The field-tier contribution requires both the general score-lifting theorem relative to the deliberately restricted bounded-ratio path class and the primitive learned-projection theorem. Until reverse score lifting is proved, the general affine projection is a candidate and every general efficiency result is explicitly conditional; the finite positive chart has an unconditional tangent calculation. The chart covers finite-support laws uniformly away from the simplex boundary and bounded exponential-tilt families with bounded statistics, but not generic dominated DQM models or paths with uncontrolled likelihood ratios. The main statistical target is the observed joint-bridge functional. It equals the causal ATE only under the separately stated latent consistency, exchangeability, positivity, negative-control, and bridge-compatibility conditions. Rank-boundary adaptation, generic compact ill-posed operators, and a full SUPPORT reanalysis remain outside scope. Under unique bijective bridge operators, the result reduces to Cui et al.'s efficient score.

seed_details.destination_search: The target-method search found source-condition double robustness for one primal-dual inverse pair but not three-way adaptation including an estimated quotient projection.
seed_details.ambition_reason: The limit law could broaden feasibility, but the projection tangent theorem should be settled before adding source-adaptive tuning.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Bennett et al.'s source-condition double robustness applies componentwise without change.
seed_details.rebuttal: Projection-space estimation creates a third inverse problem and data-dependent affine coefficients; componentwise reuse does not control their joint instability.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The identification, representative-selection, Theorem 3.4, and Corollary B.1 sections were opened. The paper already gives root-\(n\), regular, asymptotically linear estimation and local semiparametric efficiency under additional regularity for a fixed counterfactual mean; changing to treatment choice changes the derivative from that linear mean to a policy-indexed welfare process.
seed_details.question: Can a quotient-invariant proximal policy score deliver regret bounds without selecting unique bridge representatives?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Lift kernel orthogonality from one mean functional to the supremum over a policy class and derive a bridge-invariant stochastic equicontinuity bound for policy differences.
seed_details.destination_search: A direct search found a 2026 public manuscript on decision-aware proximal bridge learning and existing proximal policy-value identification, so a generic policy-regret claim is occupied or too close without a sharper decision boundary.
seed_details.ambition_reason: Policy regret would have high consumer value, but the exact nonunique quotient delta is not yet isolated from recent decision-aware work.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Recent decision-aware proximal bridge learning already controls treatment-selection regret.
seed_details.rebuttal: A quotient-efficient regret frontier may still differ, but the current search cannot defend a clean unoccupied theorem, so the seed is dropped.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: The SUPPORT construction and bridge-score inference sections were opened. The data are i.i.d. observational records with no sharp randomization null or time-permutation symmetry.
seed_details.question: Can bridge-representative invariance induce a valid finite-sample permutation or conformal orbit for the proximal ATE?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Construct a group action preserving the joint observed law and the bridge restrictions under a sharp null before inverting a bridge-residual conformity score.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found conformal proximal synthetic-control inference under time symmetry, but no exchangeability group for the cross-sectional observational ATE model; bridge nonuniqueness itself does not create randomization symmetry.
seed_details.ambition_reason: Exact coverage would be attractive, but the maintained experiment does not supply the necessary symmetry.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Permuting treatment is invalid under observational confounding, and permuting bridge representatives is not a sampling symmetry.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds, so the seed is dropped rather than repaired by adding a new experimental or time-series design.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Theorem 1, Remark 3 on covariance-aware GMM, the semiparametric comparison, and SUPPORT application were opened. Their unique finite-dimensional bridge makes the single-pair and affine-ensemble objects coincide by construction.
seed_details.question: Can one derive an observable frontier on which a regularization-selected single bridge pair and the affine ensemble are first-order equivalent, with strict divergence on the other side?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Express the variance gap as the squared distance from the quotient projection to the nonlinear single-pair coefficient variety and characterize its zero set.
seed_details.destination_search: No exact proximal frontier was found; the finite witness shows strict divergence, but a tractable observed-primitive global zero-set formula is not yet available beyond the factorization criterion.
seed_details.ambition_reason: An explicit frontier would strengthen the diagnostic, but the current kernel supports an iff factorization equation rather than a closed-form primitive threshold.
seed_details.cynical_objection: The frontier is merely the tautology that the efficient score belongs to the single-pair family.
seed_details.rebuttal: The four-corner factorization equations give nontrivial observable restrictions, but without a global closed-form threshold the seed is merged only as the attainment theorem.

literature_map: Zhang et al. (2023, Theorem 3.4 and Corollary B.1) already establish root-\(n\), regular, asymptotically linear nonunique-bridge estimation and local semiparametric efficiency under additional regularity. Bennett et al. (2026, public manuscript Theorems 3, 6, and 7) establish all-pair mixed bias and regular selected-limit inference. The new comparison is global across-pair efficiency in the simultaneous outcome- and treatment-solvability observed model, not the existence of regular inference. Chen and Xie (2026, negative-control section, observational-equivalence lemma, local-identification theorem, and Theorem 3) characterize the outcome-bridge-only model and its generalized-inverse efficient influence function; the positive witness meets their finite-support, overlap, residual-variance, bridge, and latent completeness requirements, and the joint model adds nonredundant treatment-solvability normals. Cui et al. (2024, Theorem 3.1 and SUPPORT section) provide the unique/surjective endpoint and consumer. Severini and Tripathi (2012) occupy generic quotient efficiency for underidentified NPIV. Chen and Santos (2018) provide local-overidentification geometry. Ai and Chen (2012) provide optimally weighted sequential-moment sieves. Ai and Shan (2025) provide uniquely indexed increasing-moment GMM. Imbens et al. (2025) treat unique bridges in long-term data combination. Bennett et al. (2023) provide source-condition product-rate tools. The unoccupied conditional kernel is complete score lifting for the transported joint solvability chart, the affine canonical gradient, exact nested-model and selected-pair gaps, and a feasible learned affine projection.

novelty_justification: No novelty is claimed for proximal identification, bridge nonuniqueness, root-\(n\) regular estimation, local efficiency under Zhang et al.'s additional regularity, pair-specific doubly robust inference, Hilbert projection, generalized inverses, operator subspace perturbation, or ordinary cross-fitting. The theorem-level delta is the complete tangent and normal geometry of the bounded likelihood-ratio observed-law intersection with simultaneous nonunique outcome- and treatment-bridge existence, conditional on the explicit score-lifting obligation for its actual path class, and the resulting global affine-hull canonical gradient across bridge pairs. The positive \(36\)-cell chart proves local tangent equality without that general obligation, gives the selected-pair gap \(9496288/200416125\), and gives the nested Chen--Xie outcome-only gap \(1303968/66805375\). The feasible contribution derives efficient-signal convergence from an explicit fold-specific ridge coefficient and deterministic four-corner weight map together with population approximation, foldwise bridge and residual rates, learned-dictionary error, Gram perturbations, ridge bias, exact affine constraints, coefficient envelopes, and a primitive mixed-bias product.
